messages:
Anya: Ran the cross-region bring-up comparing fast-path streaming (SSE/WebSocket) vs batch/non-stream HTTP for the new llamaX-13B-q4f16 model. Short summary chart and raw numbers here: https://internal.redwood/bench/1977777777
Anya: Test config: seq=1024, top_k=40, temp=0.2, batch sizes: streaming=concurrency 200 (fanout), non-stream batch size=32, GPUs=A100/H100, regions=us-east1, eu-west1. Quant: q4f16 on both.
Anya: Key question: where is the knee for throughput vs p50/p95 latency per region+GPU and how should we set capacity+fallbacks for hosted vs dedicated?
Sam: Nice, can you paste the short table? easier to eyeball.
Anya: Pasting minimal extract:
```
# rough tokens/sec and latencies (ms)
A100 us-east1 streaming: throughput=5200 tok/s, p50=45ms, p95=210ms
A100 us-east1 nonstream: throughput=6800 tok/s, p50=80ms, p95=320ms
H100 us-east1 streaming: throughput=7600 tok/s, p50=38ms, p95=180ms
H100 us-east1 nonstream: throughput=9800 tok/s, p50=72ms, p95=260ms
A100 eu-west1 streaming: throughput=4800 tok/s, p50=55ms, p95=260ms
A100 eu-west1 nonstream: throughput=6300 tok/s, p50=95ms, p95=360ms
```
Anya: (these are median of 5 runs, steady-state after cache warmup)
Sam: Interesting — non-stream raw throughput wins but p50 higher, streaming wins p50 but saturates earlier on p95. That matches expectations: streaming reduces overhead for short tails, batching gives better amortized kernel throughput for long sequences.
Mike: Did you try different kernel pins or triton vs native kernels? kernel choice can change the knee a lot, especially on H100.
Anya: Yes — default runtime used auto-kernel selection. I also ran a small sweep: triton-optimized vs nvfuser-custom on H100. Triton improved nonstream throughput by ~8% but increased p95 under high concurrency.
Olivia: Did quantization introduce any repeatability/quality noise at this seq len? we need to check evals before routing production traffic to q4f16.
Anya: Quick eval spot-check: 200 prompt pairs, BLEURT diff ~ -0.6 vs fp16 baseline on average. Some prompt families had bigger regressions (summarization). Flagged in the eval dashboard.
bench-bot: Automated note: end-to-end QoS test run 1977777777 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood/bench/1977777777/{charts,raw.csv}. Alerts: p95 > 300ms in eu-west1 nonstream on A100 (3/5 runs).
Sam: For capacity planning: convert tok/s to requests/sec estimate: typical gen length ~120 tokens => rps = tok/s / 120. So H100 nonstream ~81 rps per GPU, H100 streaming ~63 rps equivalent. That helps compute reserved GPU pool sizes.
Mike: For hosted fallback policy: prefer fast-path streaming for low-latency tiers (PLG free tier), but route to nonstream batch for heavy-throughput tiers or when latency SLO relaxed. Also consider region-aware routing: spin extra spare H100s in us-east for peak traffic, use A100 in eu as cheaper fallback.
Olivia: Also, add a small quality gate: if eval BLEURT drop > 0.5 on a holdout, block auto-quantized rollout. We saw borderline cases in summarization.
Anya: Follow-ups: (1) I'll run a longer 24h soak with adaptive fanout for streaming to measure long-tail p99, (2) add kernel-specific runs pinned to triton/nvfuser on both GPUs, (3) share CSV and single-plot overlay.
Sam: Sounds good. If you need quick numbers, I can convert tok/s -> GPU pool sizes for our 99th percentile traffic forecast.
bench-bot: CI note: created ticket INF-4821 for "fastpath vs batch streaming sizing" with links to artifacts.
Mike: FYI, when you run soak, enable kv-prefix-caching for repeated prefixes — that lowered p95 by ~30ms in other models.
Anya: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Olivia: +1 :thumbsup:
